chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not let his wife go to the bathhouse.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on a wife going to the public bathhouse according to hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) linking faith in the Hereafter directly to the preservation of marital modesty (haya) in public spaces. While some scholars interpret this as a recommended precaution (mustahabb) to avoid fitnah, others view it as a strong indicator of the virtue of guarding one's spouse from the gaze of others in mixed-gender environments like the hammam. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on private family dignity extending into public social interactions.
